newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-up $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-up $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, with strength expected in the eastern Corn Belt amid ongoing light marketings, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to plants could range from $57.00 to $57.50 dollars per cwt. Illinois top prices at the plant could range from $56.50 to $58.00, dealers in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant were seen ranging from $56.50 to $57.00 as packers continue to compete for cash hogs, sources there said.
Light support was tied to ideas this week's holiday-shortened slaughter would tighten fresh pork supplies and underpin prices early next week, market sources said.
Hog slaughter for the week was estimated at 1.539 million head, down 18.2 percent from last week and down 10.7 percent from last year.
Prices at midday were quoted steady on hams, $1.00 to $3.00 per cwt higher on bellies and $1.00 to $2.00 for 42 percent lean trimmings, according to USDA.
